title: Tourism corporation created and development charges approved
subtitle: Also: speed limit cuts, Gartshore Farmhouse study funding, short-term rental zoning public meeting, consent items.
overview: Council approved the framework for a new Economic Development and Tourism Municipal Services Corporation, wholly owned by the Township. It named the Mayor and Councillor Jefferson as incorporators and voting directors, authorized recruitment of public board members, and directed staff to prepare a Municipal Accommodation Tax by-law and reserve fund. The advisory committee on economic prosperity and growth was dissolved {{vote:m4}}.

Council also adopted the amended Development Charges Background Study. Current rates are frozen for six months, and a new by-law takes effect October 1, 2026. A deferral policy and local service policy were approved {{vote:m5}}. Council also endorsed speed limit reductions on five roads plus traffic calming {{vote:m6}}, and set aside up to $25,000 to assess the Gartshore Farmhouse for a change of use {{vote:m7}}.

Earlier, a public meeting on zoning changes for short-term rentals and bed and breakfasts drew concerns from residents. No decision was made, and staff will bring back a revised draft with the licensing by-law. The minutes record no matters arising from the closed session.

decisions.item: Economic Development and Tourism Municipal Services Corporation
decisions.detail: Council adopted the business case, authorized incorporation, appointed initial directors, allowed the corporation to use the 2026 Township budget, directed staff to prepare a Municipal Accommodation Tax by-law and reserve fund, and dissolved the advisory committee.

decisions.item: Development Charges Background Study and by-law
decisions.detail: Council approved the amended study, a six-month freeze at current rates, a new by-law effective October 1, 2026, a deferral policy and a local service policy.
Council endorsed proposed speed limit reductions, to be made through a speed limit by-law amendment, and directed staff to implement traffic calming measures.
Council received the update and approved up to $25,000 from the General Capital Reserve to assess upgrades needed for a change of use.
Council approved consent items including a GOST licence extension, a fire protection grant expenditure, and a Fergus BIA amending by-law.

debate: Delegates on the tourism corporation said residents were first seeing the full proposal late and that startup and operating costs lean on property taxes before accommodation tax revenue exists. They asked for more testing of the finances, and questioned the consultant's independence. Staff pointed to the surveys, open house and meetings with accommodation providers.

Development charge delegates, from a developer and a home builders' association, said the increases are too large for a slow market. They supported the six-month freeze and phase-in, and asked for more time to refine the study. Staff said growth costs fall on taxpayers and ratepayers if developers do not pay them.

Councillors discussed extending the partial intensification exemption beyond medium and high density, or lowering the five-unit threshold. Council passed the by-law as drafted after being told it could later be amended to lower charges without a new public process.

At the short-term rental zoning public meeting, delegates said redefining hotels could remove long-term rental housing, avoid licensing and safety rules, and make downtown parking rules hard to meet. One delegate raised inconsistent enforcement. Several councillors questioned the hotel definition, and staff said they would revisit it.
On speed limits, councillors raised Gordon Street and St. Andrew Street East, and asked about Eighth Line and a rural section needing review. Staff said they would monitor and collect more data.
